newsitem.title: CHINA: China, HK stage anti-illegal immigration exercise.
newsitem.headline: China, HK stage anti-illegal immigration exercise.

text.p: China and Hong Kong deployed more than 80 boats and 1,000 border police in waters around the Hong Kong-China border on Friday in an unprecedented joint exercise to combat smuggling of illegal immigrants.
About 3,500 Chinese border police were also gearing up for a large anti-smuggling exercise along the land border.

The sea exercise in Dapeng Bay was to prepare border police from both sides to cope with the tide of illegal Chinese immigrants sneaking into Hong Kong ahead of the British colony's July 1 return to China.
With Hong Kong in view on one side and China's Shenzhen city on the other, the two security forces jointly intercepted 21 fishing trawlers being used as smuggling vessels.
Smugglers, or "snakeheads" as they are known locally, use fishing trawlers and open-top speedboats to ferry Chinese migrants across to Hong Kong at night.
In the first four months of this year, 7,406 illegal migrants from China, including children, were arrested in border areas, against 23,180 for the whole of 1996.

Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region of China on July 1 after more than 150 years as a British colony. Illegal immigration has been fuelled by rumours in southern China that illegals will be granted amnesty after July 1.
The Chinese side also staged an inspection of their 19 patrol boats and 35 speedboats during the exercise.
Chinese patrol boats fired several shots as they passed a ship from which China's Deputy Minister of Public Security Tian Qiyu was observing the drills.
Tian had flown in from Beijing for the operation, which also involved three Hong Kong patrol boats and seven speedboats.

Chen Shaoji, security chief of China's Guangdong province, said he was satisfied with the drill and was confident that no mainlander would dare steal into Hong Kong after seeing the exercise, which was expected to be broadcast on Chinese television.
"Our cooperation with Hong Kong is very good. But the drill is to see whether there are any problems we can improve upon," he told reporters after the exercise.
"The figures from our side and from Hong Kong have shown human smuggling into Hong Kong is declining," he said.
At one high point of the exercise, Chinese police clambered onboard a "smuggling" boat after firing several smoke flares onto the vessel.
"Good results have been achieved in our operation and Hong Kong will have a smooth transition," Chen said.
However, he said communication with Hong Kong was one area which needed to be improved.
